model_requests.instruction:
Task: Pick the whisk from the drawer and place it on the counter.
Identify the movable source object to pick up and return its name in target. Images are ordered left camera, right camera, wrist camera. For each view, describe its appearance and give its visible center. All points must refer to that same source object. If it is not visible, set visible false and point_2d null. Use relative coordinates 0 through 1000 on each image; top-left [0,0], bottom-right [1000,1000].

right.description: A brown-handled whisk is lying inside the open drawer.

response.reason: The task is to pick the whisk from the drawer and place it on the counter. The whisk is located inside an open drawer, which is accessible from above. The 'PickPlaceCounterToDrawer-seed7' skill uses a direct vertical approach (90-degree descent), which is suitable for accessing objects in drawers. Although the skill name suggests the reverse action (counter to drawer), the parameters (direct approach, vertical descent) are the most appropriate for grasping an object from a drawer and lifting it out to place it on the counter. The other skill involves a side-horizontal approach which is less suitable for a drawer.

model_requests.instruction: Task: Pick the whisk from the drawer and place it on the counter. Verify the pickup of the task source whisk. These are three successive WRIST camera images: BEFORE closing, AFTER closing, AFTER lifting. The camera moves with the gripper. Compare the source BETWEEN THE FINGERS at the bottom of each image against the changing support surface. Does the same task source remain enclosed by the fingers after lifting? Finger separation remains 0.001m; commanded lift was 0.120m. Describe actual visual change; do not infer from the gripper command alone.

response.description: In the first image, the whisk is resting on the surface with the gripper fingers open around the handle. In the second image, the gripper has closed, enclosing the wooden handle of the whisk. In the third image, the whisk is lifted and held in the air above the counter, with the handle still firmly grasped by the gripper. The whisk remains enclosed by the fingers throughout the sequence.
